texts.facts: The present claim petition is filed under Section 166/140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter called as 'Act') by the petitioner/injured Sh. Layak Singh. Brief facts as enumerated in the petition are as given in succeeding paragraph. Layak Singh vs Hanuman Singh Rathore on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133658026/ 1 2. The accident in the present case took place on 07.01.2015. It is the case of the petitioner that on 07.01.2015, the petitioner alongwith his wife and brother was going from Delhi to Etawah by his car ECCO bearing Registration No. DL-9CL-7238 and when he reached near Balaji Mandir, Shikohabad, U.P. at about 04:00 a.m., suddenly he met with a road accident with a Container No. RJ-06G-4907, as the same was parked on road by its driver without taking any precaution and following rules regarding break down of vehicle, due to which the petitioner, his wife and brother got several serious injuries and ECCO Car was also damaged. It is further submitted that petitioner was admitted to Yashwant Nursing Home, Agra, U.P. on 07.01.2015 for his treatment in a pathetic condition and treated for the injuries at his face, leg and other parts of the body. Thus, the present claim petition was filed for compensation. 3. Respondent No. 1/Owner has filed Written Statement and stated that the present case is liable to be dismissed as no criminal case has been registered against the driver, as the petitioner himself had struck at the stationary vehicle from its back. It is further submitted that R1 had put on the parking signal light and had also placed parking triangle symbol, therefore, petitioner is not entitled to take the benefit of his own wrong. 4. Respondent 2/ IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Company Ltd. has filed its separate written statement and has taken the defence that there is no FIR lodged against driver alleging rash and negligent driving. It is further stated that the name of the driver is not known to the petitioner and he has not been made a party. It is further submitted that the GD entry was lodged, which clearly stated that there was no fault of anyone in causing the accident. It is further stated that as per GD entry, there was thick fog at the alleged accident and it is evident from the GD entry that there was no fault of insured vehicle. It is further stated that there was no written complaint lodged with the police, rather only information was given to police stating that accident occurred suddenly due to thick fog and there was no fault of anyone in the accident. Thus, there was no reason for the police to lodge any FIR, when there was no allegation of any wrongful act by the informant. It is further stated that neither the petitioner nor the respondents reside within the territorial jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court. It is further stated that neither the driver was holding a valid and effective driving licence nor had a valid permit at the time of accident. Other general defences have been taken by R2/Insurer. 5. The respondent no. 3/driver filed reply and stated that he had parked Traulla (container bearing registration No.RJ-06G-4907/ offending vehicle) due to heavy fog on the road and he had parked his vehicle on the side of the road and put the stop signal place on the back of the Traulla, but the petitioner was driving his vehicle in a very high speed and hit the respondent's traulla from the back side. The alleged accident had occurred solely due to the fault of the petitioner himself. It is further submitted that vehicle was duly insured with R2/Insurer and R-3 / driver was holding a valid and effective driving licence.

6. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties following issues were framed on 10.12.2018:-
(i) Whether Sh. Layak Singh suffered injuries in a motor vehicular accident which occurred on Layak Singh vs Hanuman Singh Rathore on 6 May, 2024

(OPP) 
(ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation , if so, to what amount and from whom?

(OPP) 
(iii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, to what rate and for which period?
(iv) Relief 7.
To prove their case, petitioner examined only one witness i.e. himself as PW1 and testified regarding the manner of accident.

He has relied upon the following documents :-

Original Medico Legal Report of petitioner issued from Yashwant Nursing Home,
Agra is Ex.PW1/7.

Original pathology report of petitioner issued from Yashwant Nursing Home, Agra is Ex.PW1/8.
 Original pathology report of petitioner issued from Yashwant Nursing Home, Agra is Ex.PW1/9.

 Original medical prescription of petitioner issued by Dr. Sanjay Gupta is Ex.PW1/11.
Original medical requisition slips in the name of petitioner issued from Yashwant Nursing Home, Agra are Ex.PW1/12 to Ex.PW1/20 respectively.

Respondent side opted not to lead evidence in their defence.

10. The issues are decided as follows:-
ISSUE No.1 11.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
12. Now in this case, the petitioner Layak Singh is the injured and witness of the accident.
In order to establish his claim, he has examined himself as PW-1.

He testified that on 07.01.2015, the petitioner alongwith his wife and brother was going from Delhi to Etawah by his car (Ecco) bearing registration No. DL-9CL-7238 and when he reached near Balaji Mandir, Shikohabad, U.P. at about 4:00 am,
It is further averred that due to this, the petitioner, his wife and brother got several serious injuries and his car was also damaged.

It is further averred that the accident took place due to rash, careless and negligent parking of the offending vehicle by driver /
R-3.
PW1 was cross-examined by Ld. Counsel for R-2 / insurer at length.
During his cross-examination, he specifically stated that he had not seen the offending vehicle parked before the accident.
He further deposed that the offending vehicle was parked on the left portion of the road and there was no traffic coming from the opposite direction but he was being followed by other vehicle.
He denied the suggestion that accident occurred due to his negligence.
13. It is relevant to mention that no FIR was registered and no investigation was taken up.

Hence,
the claim of the petitioners solely rests upon testimonies of eye-witnesses and documents on record.

In this connection, it is relevant to note that pursuant to the accident on 07.01.2015, one Rajesh Kashyap S/o- Sh. Ashok Kashyap gave an intimation to the Police Station Kotwali Shikohaband, UP (date of intimation is claimed to be 03.02.2

It was informed by him to the police that the accident took place due to sudden collusion of the car of the petitioner with the stationary container bearing registration No. RJ-06G-4907 on account of dense fog.
The informant was brother-in-law (sala) of the petitioner.

It was further submitted that injured was not interested in pursuing the remedies under Criminal Law, particularly in a different state (the injured is stated to be a resident of Delhi) and hence, no effort was made by them for registration

It was further submitted that as the petitioner was resident of Delhi, he would have faced hardship in Layak Singh vs Hanuman Singh Rathore on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133658026/
4 pursuing the case in U.P. an
At the outset, it is observed that mere non-registration of FIR is not fatal to the case of petitioner.

Moving forward, it is seen that the delayed statement by brother in law of injured /
petitioner suggests that the accident occurred due to dense fog and no negligence was attributed to anyone.

The medico-legal report of the Yashwant Nursing Home, Agra, U.P. dated 07.01.2015 mentions that 'alleged sustained injuries due to road side accident on 07.01.2015 and hence, it is clear that the matter was reported to the doctor as a road
There is nothing in the medical documents to dispute this claim.
Hence, it is clear that petitioner sustained injuries in a road accident.
In his affidavit, petitioner / PW1 deposed that accident took place due to wrong parking of the offending vehicle.
He further averred in his testimony that the said offending vehicle was parked without taking any precaution and following traffic rules regarding break down of vehicle.
Respondents No.1 and 2 did not bother to led any evidence in their defence to shatter the case of the petitioner.

Furthermore, there is no evidence or proof on record which could reflect that the offending vehicle was parked on the side of the road with parking signal and halting sign and to show that necessary precautions as claimed in the written sta
Respondents no. 1 and 2 did not led any evidence even to suggest why the vehicle was so parked on roadside.
From the testimonies of PW1, it is clear that respondent No.1 was negligent and did not take due care to avoid collision.
It is the plea of R2 that accident took place due to the sole negligence of Petitioner.
R-2 stated in his written submission that accident took place on Yamuna Express highway which is a three-lane dual carriageway and wide enough to carry many vehicles.
It is submitted that since the petitioner did not see the vehicle parked before the accident, he himself was negligent.
The Tribunal do not find any force in the aforesaid contention.
R2 has not disputed the factum of occurrence of accident.
Admittedly, incident took place in the winters in early morning hours.

The document Ex. PW-1/3 reveals that there was dense fog at the time of accident and offending vehicle was parked on the roadside and due to fog, vehicle of petitioner collided with the offending vehicle.

During his examination-in-chief by way of affidavit Ex. PW-1/A, petitioner claimed that he met with road accident as offending vehicle was parked on road by its driver without taking any precaution and following traffic rules.
Petitioner claimed that accident took place due to careless and negligent parking of the offending vehicle as its driver failed to take due care and precaution.

During his cross-examination, petitioner stood firm on his claim and deposed that offending vehicle was parked on the left portion of the road and he had not seen the parked offending vehicle before the accident.
A suggestion was given to the petitioner that accident occurred due to his negligence, which was denied by the petitioner.
It is not clarified as to how the petitioner himself was negligent in the occurrence of alleged accident.
Even no plea of contributory negligence of petitioner was taken on behalf of respondents during pendency of this enquiry and raised for the first time during arguments.
It was not disputed that offending vehicle was parked on the road side at the time of accident.
As per rule 15 of Road Rule Regulations, no vehicle is to be parked on the main road or one carrying fast traffic.
In this case, accident took place on the main road meant for carrying fast traffic.

R-1 did not enter into witness box to explain the reason for parking his vehicle on the road side of a busy road and what precaution he had taken to avert the possibility of any untoward incident due to his parking of offending vehicle on a
Thus, the negligence of driver of offending vehicle in parking his vehicle on the busy road in foggy morning is evident from the facts itself.

No contributory negligence can be attributed upon the petitioner as he was driving his Layak Singh vs Hanuman Singh Rathore on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133658026/
5 car with head lights on.
No suggestion was given to PW-1 that he was driving the car in high speed or that he was not following the traffic rules and due to his contributory negligence, the accident took place.

Thus, the judgment titled as Raj Rani & Ors. vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd & Ors., 2009 (13)
SCC 654 is not applicable to the fact and circumstances of present case as no act or omission on the part of claimant has been brought on record t

In the case at hand, petitioner has duly proved that R-3 was negligent in parking his vehicle on roadside without any cogent reason and without taking necessary precautions and R-3 failed to lead any evidence to suggest otherwise.
Hence, no contributory negligence can be attributed to the petitioner.

Civil Appeal No.
7300-7309 of 2016 decided on 09.02.2018.
14.

On considering the afore-said testimonies of petitioner, the police investigation report and the supporting material on record, it is found that the manner of accident and involvement of the offending vehicle and its being parked in neglige
In view of this Court, afore-said material is found sufficient to establish that the accident had occurred due to wrong parking of offending vehicle resulting in injuries to petitioner.
Therefore, issue no.1 is decided in favour of the petitioner/s and against all of the respondents.
ISSUE No.2 15.
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
16. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.

It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured ,
comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injur

Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disabilit
The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.

If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though he may be awarded Layak Singh vs Hanuman Singh Rathore on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon

Therefore, on the basis of the injuries to the petitioner, the compensation is awarded to him under the aforesaid heads as follows :-
MEDICAL EXPENSES:
17.
Petitioner has proved on record his original medical bills Ex.PW1/10, Ex. PW1/12 to Ex. PW1/24 to the tune of Rs.62,541/-.
Document Ex.PW1/25 and Ex. PW1/26 are advance payment receipts and not bills and must be part of final bill and cannot being counted separately.

Under this head,
actual medical bills are reimbursed.
All the bills are in original and in order.
No serious dispute has been raised with respect to the said medical bills on behalf of respondents.
Therefore, I award Rs.62,541/- as compensation under this head.

PAIN AND SUFFERING:
18.
According to his affidavit, after the accident, petitioner was got admitted in Yashwant Nursing Home Agra, U.P. on 07.01.2015 and remained admitted there till 12.01.2015.
The medico-legal report of the petitioner Ex.PW1/7 prepared at Yashwant Nursing Home reflects that the petitioner received grievous injuries in the accident.
The document Ex. PW1/7 also suggest that petitioner received head injuries.

Discharge Card of Yashwant Nursing Home Ex. PW1/6 clearly reflects that petitioner remained hospitalized from 07.01.2015 to 12.01.2015 and during his hospitalization,
certain tests and procedure were done.
Considering the nature of injuries, it can be readily inferred that petitioner must have remained under considerable pain and suffering due to the accident.
Hence, I find it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs.30,000/- to the petitioner under this head.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 19.
The petitioner has not proved any actual expenses in relation to these heads and has not placed any material on record to substantiate the said expenses.
In the given facts and circumstances of the case, I deem it fit to grant Rs.10,000/- to petitioner for conveyance and Rs.10,000/- under the head of special diet.
20. Though petitioner has claimed attendant expenses, no evidence has been led to show that petitioner had hired any attendant during her treatment.

It cannot be ignored that family members of petitioner must have had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner for her routine activities and that would definitely suffer their work/job.

For claiming compensation,
necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the
(DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
Therefore, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- as attendant charges.
21. Thus, petitioner is granted a total compensation of Rs.30,000/- (10,000+10,000+10,000) under this head.

7 LOSS OF INCOME DURING TREATMENT :
22.

In his affidavit of evidence Ex. PW1/A, petitioner has claimed that he was running his shop of repairing work / mechanic work of Gas Stove etc in Kailash Nagar, Delhi and also working as a part time driver and from both the profession, he w
No documentary evidence has been produced by him in this regard.
Petitioner has also not proved on record his educational documents.
In his testimony, he has deposed that he was doing the job of driver, however, he has not summoned any witness to substantiate his plea.

He has also not proved on record his driving licence or any other document which could corroborate his version that he is a driver by profession In the absence of proof of his income and special skill, income of the petitioner is taken as p

The minimum wages for unskilled worker as applicable in the Delhi on the date of accident i.e.
07.01.2015 was Rs. 8632/- per month.

As per the discharge card Ex.PW1/6, petitioner remained hospitalized for about 5-6 days, however, there is nothing in the medical document to suggest that bed-rest was prescribed for him for any particular period of time.
It is not difficult to presume that petitioner who suffered head injuries, must have been disabled from work for at least two months.
Therefore, I award Rs.17,264/- (8632x2) as compensation under this head.

23. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarized as under:-
 Sl. No. Head of compensation Amount  1 Medical Expenses Rs.62,541/-
 2 Pain & Sufferings Rs.30,000/-
 3 Conveyance & Special diet Rs.20,000/-
 4 Attendant charge
Petitioner has pursued his case diligently since 2016.

Therefore, he is entitled for interest @
7.5% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.

LIABILITY:
25.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.
As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured, the Insurance company is liable to compensate the third party.
In view of above, it is held that respondent no.2/ insurer shall be entitled to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.

26. In view of the findings on above points, I as presiding officer of this Tribunal award a total compensation of Rs. 1,40,000/- (rupees one lakh forty Thousand only) along with interest @ 7.5%
per annum on the aforesaid award amount from
This award is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.
